stateGlyphs.loading: open ring (static arc under reduced motion)

roleDescriptions.divider: Decorative hairline between regions of one surface (group gaps, list/detail split, sidebar edge). Never the only indication of an interactive boundary; below 3:1 by design.
roleDescriptions.controlBorder: Boundary of editable fields, checkboxes, radios and segmented controls where the outline identifies the control. Measured 3.06–4.77:1 (dark) and 3.11–3.74:1 (light) against background/surface/raised/selection. Baseline border stays for decorative containers.
roleDescriptions.selectionRail: 2 px vertical rail inset 4 px inside the selected row/cell/node. Same value as accent; >=4.6:1 against selection in both themes. Always paired with the neutral selection surface and aria-selected, never alone.
roleDescriptions.userMessage: Subdued surface for user chat turns. Assistant prose stays on surface without a container.
roleDescriptions.toolSurface: Collapsible tool-activity and approval blocks in chat and workflow debug output.
roleDescriptions.canvas: Workflow canvas field and other pannable workspaces.
roleDescriptions.canvasDot: 16 px dot grid on canvas. Decorative.
roleDescriptions.scrim: Behind modal confirmation only. Not used behind the transient launcher.
roleDescriptions.tintDanger: Inline error/destructive-confirmation band. danger text keeps >=7:1 (dark) / >=5.7:1 (light).
roleDescriptions.tintSuccess: Inline success confirmation. Never used for simulated results.
roleDescriptions.glyphTiles: 20 px rounded (radius.keycap) glyph tiles behind white 1.5 px stroke icons. White glyph contrast 4.61–5.58:1 on every tile. Hue aids scanning only; type is also given by glyph shape and text accessory.
roleDescriptions.glyphOnTile: Stroke colour for icons drawn on glyph tiles.

proposal.scope: Applies to the shared host primitives (Row, GroupCaption, GlyphTile, Keycap, ShortcutHint, ActionPanel, Footer, StatePlate, Workspace frame) and the declarative ViewRenderer. Extensions and workflow packages may select a glyphTiles category for their commands; they cannot supply colours, CSS or custom components.
